Class WindowEngine

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.window.WindowEngine
public final class WindowEngine extends Object
The resolution engine of THE ONE WINDOW: one store, one cascade, one method, resolve(Address, BehaviorKey). It never branches on KindTag; it walks the declarations for an address and returns a fully resolved value, never null.

One store with a tier axis (§0063)

Every declaration lives in the store for its key's Tier. A SERVER key (what a slot accepts, the operations, reactions with authority) is held and resolved in the server tier; a CLIENT key (visibility, opacity, observed reactions) in the client tier. The two tiers are one data structure walked by one algorithm; they differ only in which levels they have. Until 6.0.0 the server tier was a second copy of this class in Containers.

The cascade

  1. Per address: a declaration on the thing itself.
  2. Owner chain (client tier only): a declaration on an ancestor, the panel a slot or element hangs under, nearest first. "Set opacity once on the panel" flows to everything inside.
  3. Groups: every group the address is a member of, by GroupKey.precedence() (a slot group over its category). A tie at one precedence goes to the group whose id sorts last, never to the one registered last: registration order is mod load order, which Fabric does not define.
  4. The key's BehaviorKey.libraryDefault().
A Decl.Set stops the walk. Decl.Inherit is not stored: writing it removes the declaration, so clearing a slot leaves nothing behind and the store does not grow per player or per block.

Threading

Declarations and resolution may race (the client thread and the integrated server both use the engine). The maps are concurrent, the group lists are copy-on-write, group creation is serialised, and every Decl is immutable, so a resolve racing a write sees the old value or the new one.

      resolve(Address, BehaviorKey) with memberships the caller knows and the address alone does not say.
